title: Safety and efficacy of delpacibart zotadirsen in Duchenne muscular dystrophy mutations amenable to exon 44 skipping in the USA (EXPLORE44): a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase 1/2 trial
title_zh: Delpacibart Zotadirsen在美国可进行44号外显子跳跃的杜氏肌营养不良症突变中的安全性与疗效（EXPLORE44）：一项随机、安慰剂对照、双盲、I/II期临床试验
abstract: BACKGROUND: There are no approved exon skipping therapies to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy due to DMD variants amenable to exon 44 skipping (DMD44). Delpacibart zotadirsen (del-zota, also known as AOC 1044) is a first-in-class antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate designed to deliver an exon 44-skipping phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer to muscle to restore dystrophin expression for individuals with DMD44. EXPLORE44 was a first-in-human trial to evaluate del-zota's safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy. METHODS: EXPLORE44 was a two-part randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 1/2 study in healthy adult men (aged 18-55 years; part A) and ambulatory and non-ambulatory male participants with DMD44 (aged 7-27 years; part B) at ten clinical research sites in the USA. Dosing in part B was informed by safety, pharmacokinetic, and pharmacodynamic data from part A. In part B, participants with DMD44 were randomised (3:1 del-zota:placebo) within two dose cohorts to receive three intravenous doses of del-zota (5 mg/kg every 6 weeks, or 10 mg/kg every 8 weeks) or matching placebo. A computer-generated permuted-block randomisation schedule was prepared by an independent statistician with no further role in the study. Infusions were prepared by an unmasked pharmacist under supervision of the masked investigator; other site staff, participants, and sponsor team members were masked to allocation. The primary objective was safety and tolerability measured by the incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events. Secondary endpoints assessing target engagement were change from baseline in exon skipping (ie, defined as the percentage of dystrophin mRNA transcripts in which exon 44 is excluded from the mature mRNA relative to total dystrophin mRNA transcripts) and dystrophin level to month 4 (5 mg/kg cohort) or month 5 (10 mg/kg cohort). The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05670730) and is complete. FINDINGS: Between Dec 5, 2022, and June 27, 2024, we enrolled and randomly assigned 45 healthy volunteers and 26 men and boys with DMD44. In part A, three (30%) of ten healthy volunteers who received placebo and 21 (62%) of 34 who received del-zota reported at least one adverse event, none of which were severe or serious. In part B, nine participants with DMD44 received del-zota at 5 mg/kg, ten at 10 mg/kg, and seven received placebo; mean age 13·3 years (SD 4·2). 16 (84%) participants with DMD44 treated with del-zota and six (86%) treated with placebo reported at least one adverse event, most of which were mild or moderate; two participants, both in the 5 mg/kg del-zota group, discontinued due to adverse events (anaphylactic reaction and infusion-related reaction). Mean increases from baseline in exon 44 skipping were 36·6% (95% CI 20·8 to 52·4, SD 17·1, nominal p=0·0013) at 5 mg/kg, 43·4% (32·8 to 54·0, 14·9, nominal p<0·0001) at 10 mg/kg, and 1·6% (-3·4 to 6·7, 4·8, nominal p=0·44) with placebo. Mean increases from baseline in dystrophin levels were 25·0% (9·2 to 40·7, 17·0, nominal p=0·0082) at 5 mg/kg, 25·6% (13·0 to 38·3, 17·7, nominal p=0·0013) at 10 mg/kg, and -0·7% (-4·8 to 3·3, 3·9, nominal p=0·66) with placebo. INTERPRETATION: Del-zota had an acceptable safety profile, produced increases in exon 44 skipping and dystrophin expression, and decreased biomarkers of muscle damage in participants with DMD44. Findings from this study support further investigation of del-zota in a phase 3 study to assess efficacy and long-term safety. FUNDING: Avidity Biosciences, A Novartis Company.
abstract_zh: 背景：目前尚无获批的外显子跳跃疗法可治疗因DMD基因可进行44号外显子跳跃（DMD44）而导致的杜氏肌营养不良症。Delpacibart Zotadirsen（del‑zota，亦称AOC 1044）是一种首创的抗体-寡核苷酸偶联物，旨在将44号外显子跳跃的磷酸二胺基形态胺寡核苷酸递送至肌肉，以恢复DMD44患者的肌营养不良蛋白表达。EXPLORE44是首个人体试验，评估del‑zota的安全性、耐受性、药代动力学、药效学及疗效。方法：EXPLORE44为两部分、随机、双盲、安慰剂对照、I/II期研究，分别在美国十家临床研究中心招募健康成年男性（18-55岁；A组）和可行走与不可行走的DMD44男性参与者（7-27岁；B组）。B组的剂量设定基于A组的安全性、药代动力学和药效学数据。B组中，DMD44患者按3:1比例随机分配（del‑zota:安慰剂）进入两剂量组，接受三次静脉注射del‑zota（5 mg/kg每6周或10 mg/kg每8周）或匹配安慰剂。随机化方案由独立统计学家生成，且在研究中不再参与。输注由未遮蔽的药剂师在遮蔽研究者监督下准备；其他现场工作人员、参与者及赞助方成员均保持遮蔽。主要终点为安全性与耐受性，评估标准为治疗相关不良事件发生率。次要终点包括目标受体结合评估：44号外显子跳跃率（即排除44号外显子的肌营养不良蛋白mRNA相对于总mRNA的百分比）及至第4个月（5 mg/kg组）或第5个月（10 mg/kg组）的肌营养不良蛋白水平变化。试验已在ClinicalTrials.gov注册（NCT05670730），并已完成。结果：2022年12月5日至2024年6月27日，我们共招募并随机分配45名健康志愿者和26名DMD44男性及男孩。A组中，10名健康志愿者中有3名（30%）接受安慰剂、34名接受del‑zota的志愿者中有21名（62%）报告至少一次不良事件，均为轻度或中度，未见严重或危及生命事件。B组中，9名DMD44患者接受5 mg/kg、10名接受10 mg/kg、7名接受安慰剂；平均年龄13.3岁（SD 4.2）。接受del‑zota的DMD44患者中有16名（84%）报告至少一次不良事件，接受安慰剂的6名（86%）亦报告不良事件，绝大多数为轻度或中度；两名5 mg/kg组患者因不良事件（过敏性反应和输注相关反应）停药。44号外显子跳跃率相对基线的平均增幅为5 mg/kg组36.6%（95% CI 20.8–52.4，SD 17.1，p=0.0013），10 mg/kg组43.4%（32.8–54.0，SD 14.9，p<0.0001），安慰剂组1.6%（-3.4–6.7，SD 4.8，p=0.44）。肌营养不良蛋白水平相对基线的平均增幅为5 mg/kg组25.0%（9.2–40.7，SD 17.0，p=0.0082），10 mg/kg组25.6%（13.0–38.3，SD 17.7，p=0.0013），安慰剂组-0.7%（-4.8–3.3，SD 3.9，p=0.66）。结论：del‑zota具有可接受的安全性，显著提高44号外显子跳跃率和肌营养不良蛋白表达，并降低DMD44患者的肌肉损伤生物标志物。本研究结果支持进一步在III期试验中评估del‑zota的疗效与长期安全性。资助：Avidity Biosciences，Novartis公司。
